card.title: Why prisms paint rainbows — dispersive power

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Refractive index falls with wavelength (Cauchy: μ = A + B/λ²), so violet bends more than red and white light fans into VIBGYOR — dispersion. A PURE spectrum has no gaps or overlaps (achieved with proper slit + collimation). The same μ(λ) shifts every lens focus by colour (chromatic aberration) and spherical surfaces blur marginal rays (spherical aberration); cementing crown + flint glass cancels colour error — achromatism.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Cauchy: μ = A + B/λ² (μ_violet > μ_red)  ·  dispersive power ω = (μ_v − μ_r)/(μ_y − 1)  ·  angular dispersion = δ_v − δ_r  ·  achromatic doublet: ω₁/F₁ + ω₂/F₂ = 0 (opposite lenses, balanced powers)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Dispersion analysis needs the prism near minimum deviation per colour (else geometry muddies the physics). Pure spectrum demands a narrow slit, collimated beam and clean optics. Achromatism cancels TWO wavelengths exactly (usually red/blue) — the rest (secondary spectrum) only shrinks.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Rainbow: dispersion + TIR + refraction inside droplets. Flint glass disperses ~2× crown — hence the doublet pairing. Newton recombined the spectrum with a second inverted prism, proving white light is composite, not prism-stained. Camera lenses stack 5+ elements to tame both aberrations.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Why does white light split in glass? Each colour carries its own μ (Cauchy), so Snell's bend differs per wavelength: violet (short λ, high μ) deviates most, red least — the prism sorts light by wavelength into seven bands (NEB 2022, 3 marks). No new physics beyond μ(λ) + refraction.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Cauchy's formula is empirical (fails near absorption bands — anomalous dispersion). A doublet achromatises two colours, never all. Spherical aberration needs aspheric surfaces or stops, not just glass choice — colour and shape errors are independent enemies.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Prism deviation δ ≈ (μ−1)A (small angle) differs per colour: angular spread = (μ_v − μ_r)A. Dividing by mean deviation (μ_y−1)A isolates the material property ω = (μ_v−μ_r)/(μ_y−1) — geometry cancels, leaving pure dispersive power. Doublet condition follows from zeroing total spread: ω₁δ₁ + ω₂δ₂ = 0 with opposite lens signs.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: VIBGYOR order = decreasing deviation = decreasing μ: violet bends most. 'Why disperse?' → one line: μ depends on λ. Achromatism = crown convex + flint concave cemented, powers in inverse ω ratio.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2022 (3): what is dispersion + why white light splits into seven colours in glass. NEB 2023 (4): derive i–e–A–δ relation through a prism. Dispersive power definition and achromatism applications round it out.
